title: Starship (V3 ship)
note: SpaceX Starship V3 (Block 3) ship, the upper stage, as first flown on Flight 12 (ship S39; SpaceX photo names), on its own without the booster. Dry, unfuelled (no frost). Frame: z up, the ship's base (aft skirt) at z = 0, the axis on x = y = 0. +x is the windward (heat-shield) side, which faces away from the launch tower; -x faces the tower. y completes a right-handed frame. No reference 3D model exists (see reference_model): the layout comes from the sources below and from SpaceX photos, scaled by the 9 m diameter. The booster is its own model (superheavy).

reference_model.note: Searched gh api repos/nasa/NASA-3D-Resources on 2026-10-28: no SpaceX vehicle. No official 3D model. NASA's 3D Resources has no Starship; the models online are third-party marketplace models, not sources.

height.quote: No source states the V3 ship's height. wiki_starship gives the Block 2 ship as "Block 2 : 52.1 m (171 ft)", the same number; the derivation assumes the ship sits on top of the booster without overlap.

conflict.quote: measured: nose tip to the top of the hot-stage ring 427 px against an 80.5 px body width (9 m). photo_pad_f13_close gives 49.4 m. Both are likely shortened by perspective (see open_questions).

measured: nose tip (y 184) to the top of the hot-stage ring (y 496.5), 312.5 px, against the ship's width of 53.5 px (9 m), which stays the same along the ship, so perspective doesn't change the scale over it. Agrees with 52.1 m within 1%.

stack_height.quote: Block 1 : 121.3 m (398 ft) Block 2 : 123.1 m (404 ft) Block 3 : 124.4 m (408 ft)

also.quote: Fully stacked with its booster, the rocket is 408 feet (124 meters) tall.

booster_height.quote: Super Heavy was initially 71 m (233 ft) tall (in its Block 1 and Block 2 design, now retired), while Block 3 Super Heavy is 72.3 meters tall.

also.quote: The stainless-steel booster stands 236 feet tall (72 meters) and boasts a diameter of 9 m (29.5 ft).

ship_engines.quote: Block 3 Ship will not have nine engines right away, but will stick with six, meaning three Raptor Vacuum (RVACs) and three Raptor Sea Level or Center (RC) engines.
ship_engines.also: SpaceX's photo of S39 is named "S39_6-Engine_Static_Fire"; wiki_starship: "The three sea level engines are mounted on the thrust puck, which forms the bottom of the aft dome."
ship_engines.note: wiki_starship_ship (secondary) says the six engines "are housed within a dedicated shielding compartment": inside the skirt, as render_aft_b3 shows.

no_engine_shrouds.quote: Large individual engine shrouds have been eliminated ... Sensors and controllers are now internally integrated and covered by engine thermal protection, eliminating the need for individual engine shrouds on both Starship and Super Heavy.

ship_flaps.value: 2 forward and 2 aft flaps. Forward flaps on the leeward side, about 140 degrees apart; aft flaps 180 degrees apart (on +y and -y).
ship_flaps.quote: Beginning with Block 2, the design of these forward flaps was significantly changed, moving leeward and becoming thinner and angled. This sets them at an approximately 140-degree angle, compared to the 180-degree angle of the aft flaps
ship_flaps.also: spacex_v3: "The aft flap actuation system has also been upgraded from two actuators per flap to a single actuator with three motors."

heat_shield.value: black hexagonal tiles on the windward side (+x), the top of the nose and round the forward flaps' roots; the rest of the leeward side is bare stainless steel (layout in from_photos.tile_layout)
heat_shield.quote: wiki_starship: "The windward side is protected by a heat shield composed of eighteen thousand hexagonal black tiles". photo_s39_fire shows the windward side black from nose to skirt; photo_wdr shows the leeward side bare steel with the tile edge just in view.

ring_height.quote: These cylinders have a height of 1.83 m (6 ft), and a thickness of 3.97 mm (0.156 in).
ring_height.note: Weld lines every 1.83 m show on the steel in every photo: a texture detail, not geometry.

docking_drogues.quote: Four docking drogues have also been added on the leeward side of the vehicles to enable docking with other Starships
docking_drogues.note: Not visible at site scale; listed only.

ship_catch_pins.quote: SpaceX has refined the design of the ship catch pins and relocated them to the nosecone.

raptor_sl_nozzle_exit_m.quote: Nozzle exit diameter (in) 51.226 ... Nozzle throat to exit length (in) 60.06
raptor_sl_nozzle_exit_m.note: Raptor 1-era (2019) sea-level nozzle; nothing found for Raptor 3. 51.226 in = 1.301 m; throat to exit 60.06 in = 1.526 m.

scale.source: photo_pad_f13: ship and booster both 80.5 px wide (9 m). Along the axis the photo reads short against the ascent photo (ship 47.7 m vs 52.6 m), so it seems squashed vertically: lengths there are scaled by the 52.1 m ship (0.122 m/px), widths by the diameter (0.1118 m/px). The hot-stage ring then measures 3.8 m, matching nsf_pad2's 'nearly four-meter' ring.

nose_length.source: photo_pad_f13: the nose reaches the full 9 m width about 93 px below the tip. Estimated.

nose_tip_radius.source: photo_pad_f13: the tip's width over its first 1.5 m (0.9 to 2.9 m wide at 0.2 to 1.5 m below the tip) fits a sphere of radius 0.9 to 1.5 m; 1.2 m, tangent to the ogive. Estimated.

forward_flap.source: photo_pad_f13: the -y forward flap stands out 20 px from the body (2.2 m), seen about 20 degrees off its plane (flaps 140 degrees apart, viewed from the windward side), so about 2.4 m; root from y 125 to 178, outer edge y 160 to 177; bottom 76 px below the tip. Estimated. Shape: swept leading edge, straight outer edge (photo_wdr).

aft_flap.source: photo_pad_f13: the -y flap stands out 18 px (2.0 m), the +y one 16.5 px (1.85 m); root from y 410 to the ship's base at y 529, outer edge from y 465 down. Estimated. photo_wdr and photo_pad_f13 both show the aft flaps reaching slightly below the ship's base, alongside the hot-stage ring. Tip chord revised: in photo_wdr (aft flap crop x 2400-2760, y 1400-1860) the outer edge is 0.65 of the root (210 px of 325 px), so 0.65 x 14.5 = 9.4 m; the pad photo's 7.6 m read the edge's dark part only.

aft_flap_housing.source: photo_wdr (aft flap crop): a dark angular block on the body at the top of the flap's root, about 50 px tall (2.1 m at 0.0428 m/px) and about 25 px (1 m) out. Estimated. Shape: a steel wedge whose top slopes down outward, the outer edge about half the height at the body (photo_wdr, aft flap crop). Material: bare steel in the same crop.

tile_layout.unit: m, degrees from the windward side (+x)
tile_layout.source: photo_wdr (leeward side; nose crop x 2440-2800, y 540-1100): the top of the nose is black all round down to about y 615 (tip y 557); around the forward flaps the black wraps onto the leeward side, to about 118 degrees, down to y 830; below that only a strip at the left limb is black. With the ship's length scaled to 52.1 m (0.0428 m/px along it): tip cap 2.5 m, wrap down to 11.6 m below the tip. The camera's azimuth, 45-55 degrees off the leeward side (from the forward flap's position and the strip's width), puts the barrel's boundary at about 90 degrees, along the aft flaps' roots, as in the Flight 13 onboard view (Flight_13_Onboards_07272601927.jpg). Estimated.

hex_tiles.source: photo_wdr: a tiled patch on the leeward side (x 2578-2662, y 1402-1466): the pattern repeats every 7 px across (tile centres in a row) and about 12 px up (two staggered rows), i.e. hexagons with a vertex up, 7 px x 0.0366 m/px = 0.26 m across the flats; fitted to 0.2618 m so 108 tiles go round. The gaps are 1.87 times as bright as the tiles there (sRGB means of the brightest 15% and darkest 30% of pixels). Gap width (12 mm), tile-to-tile shade spread are estimated: they're under a pixel in every photo. Edge bevel (12 mm), gap depth (8 mm) and each tile's random tilt (up to 0.07, about 4 degrees, in the normal map) are estimated, chosen so the tiles catch light one by one as they do in photo_s39_fire and photo_wdr. The texture repeats every 12 x 12 tiles (9 repeats round), each tile with its own shade and tilt, so the shading doesn't visibly repeat. No white replacement tiles: photo_s39_fire shows only specks smaller than a tile (chips or frost), 0.01% of the barrel's pixels brighter than sRGB 120.

weld_lines.source: photo_wdr: the weld lines between the 1.83 m steel rings show in every photo but are under a pixel wide; line width (20 mm) and how dark (0.8 as bright as the steel) estimated.

source: render_aft_b3, seen from below: the skirt's open end is 580 px across at the 1400 px view (9 m, 0.0155 m/px). Sea-level bells 83 px (1.29 m, agreeing with faa_plume's 1.30 m), their centres about 0.9 m from the axis in a triangle; vacuum bells 155-162 px (2.45 m), centres 3.2-3.3 m out (3.2 so they clear the skirt wall); all recessed inside the skirt, the vacuum bells' exits nearly at its edge, the sea-level ones higher. The render has six vacuum bells (a later nine-engine ship); V3 has three (facts.ship_engines), in every other slot. Which three, and how the layout is clocked against the flaps, isn't shown: built with a sea-level engine toward +x and the vacuum bells between them. Exit heights, bay depth and wall thickness estimated.
photo_hotstage (a V3 ship, the six engines from the hot-stage ring before launch): the sea-level bells' exits about level with the vacuum bells', so sl_exit_above_base 0.2 like the vacuum ones'.

photo_ship_underside: the bay's ceiling is the aft dome, a plate of bolted panels; the sea-level engines hang from its centre and the vacuum engines from its slope, so aft_dome runs from the sea-level engines' tops up its slope past the vacuum engines' tops to the skirt (heights below).
raptor3_spec: the sea-level engine is 2.94 m tall; with its exit at 0.2 m its top is at 3.14, so aft_dome's flat centre at 3.15.

raptor3vac_spec: the vacuum engine is 4.74 m tall; with its exit at 0.2 m its top is at 4.94 at r 3.2 (the dome there about 4.8, the engine's cap sitting in it); the dome meets the skirt at bay_depth 5.05. Its shape between estimated.

photo_ship_underside: about a dozen stiffening rings round the inside of the skirt (skirt_rings, spacing and size estimated); a heavy bracket on the skirt wall 27 degrees either side of each vacuum bell (centre 380 px out at 65 and 119 degrees round the 742 px skirt, the top vacuum bell at 91), size estimated.
photo_ship_underside: which way each engine's pump faces isn't seen; sea-level pumps outward, vacuum pumps inward (away from the skirt wall), estimated.

flap_hinges.unit: m, brackets as fractions along the root
flap_hinges.source: render_aft_b3 (full size, 0.0085 m/px; the aft flaps are edge-on there): each aft flap's root edge stands about 60 px (0.5 m) off the body, joined by brackets about 30 px (0.25 m) thick, with a thin rod (about 15 px, 0.13 m across) between flap and body. photo_wdr shows a bracket at the forward flaps' roots too, closer to the nose. Bracket count and spacing estimated (the render shows only the lower end of the aft flap).

catch_pins.unit: m, degrees either side of the tower side (-x)
catch_pins.source: photo_wdr (nose crop x 2510-2810, y 640-990): two stubby steel cylinders with dark end faces stick out where the nose meets the barrel, centre at y 902 (tip y 557, 0.0428 m/px along: 14.8 m below the tip), about 22 px (0.9 m) across. Taken as the catch pins nsf_block3_moon puts on the nose cone (inferred: not labelled). One points almost at the camera (45-55 degrees off the leeward side, see tile_layout) and the other is on the far limb, the near one 5 px left of the axis (2 degrees), at about 141 degrees, so they sit about 39 degrees either side of the tower side. Length estimated. Corrected (2026-10-28): the camera looks along about 143 degrees, not 130. The two raceways, which sit 40 degrees apart in this photo, are mirrored about the tower side (a scale model of the ship seen from the tower side, user's photo), so the camera is at 180 - (17 + 56) / 2 = 143 degrees; every angle read from this photo moves by +13 degrees.

tile_edge.value: jagged: the tiles stop on whole hexagons, so the edge follows the tiles' sides and steps half a tile every row
tile_edge.source: photo_s36 (a V2 ship, the clearest view of the edge): the boundary between the tiles and the bare steel steps along the hexagons on the nose and the barrel. Built on the barrel's two edges (+-90 degrees); the flap-wrap and nose-cap edges stay straight.

raceways.source: photo_wdr (pipes crop x 2640-2780, y 880-1180, and the aft crop): two steel covers run down the leeward side, flat-faced, about 20 px (0.75 m at 0.0383 m/px across) wide, with pointed tops level with the catch pins (y 905 and 925: 14.9 and 15.7 m below the tip at 0.0428 m/px) and ending just above the aft skirt (about y 1690, 48.5 m below the tip). Across the 235 px body (centre x 2647) they sit 34 px and 98 px right of the axis, 17 and 56 degrees round from the camera; with the camera looking along 143 degrees that puts them at 160 and 200 degrees. How far they stand out is estimated. The clamps that give older ships' raceways a ladder look aren't visible under the frost here, so they aren't modelled. Corrected (2026-10-28): the camera looks along about 143 degrees, not 130. The two raceways, which sit 40 degrees apart in this photo, are mirrored about the tower side (a scale model of the ship seen from the tower side, user's photo), so the camera is at 180 - (17 + 56) / 2 = 143 degrees; every angle read from this photo moves by +13 degrees.

tile_patches.unit: m, degrees either side of the tower side (-x)
tile_patches.source: photo_wdr: black tiled squares on the bare steel. Nose crop: one at x 2615-2670, y 1025-1080 (2.1 x 2.35 m, 21.2 m below the tip), almost facing the camera (about 141 degrees); aft crop: one at x 2575-2665, y 1395-1472 (3.4 x 3.3 m, 37.5 m below the tip, about 135 degrees). Both have a partner showing at the far limb at about the same height, so they are taken as mirrored about the tower side, like the catch pins. How far the tiles stand proud of the steel is estimated. Corrected (2026-10-28): the camera looks along about 143 degrees, not 130. The two raceways, which sit 40 degrees apart in this photo, are mirrored about the tower side (a scale model of the ship seen from the tower side, user's photo), so the camera is at 180 - (17 + 56) / 2 = 143 degrees; every angle read from this photo moves by +13 degrees.

ports.source: photo_wdr: dark round openings on the leeward steel at (x, y) 2727,921 (15 px, 0.57 m); 2658,987 and 2632,986 (a pair, 7 px); 2649,637 on the nose (8 px, 0.3 m); 2600,1210 (6 px, 0.22 m); 2595,1568; 2635,1598; 2571,1746 (7-8 px, 0.26-0.29 m); and a dark square on the nose at 2658,752 (17 px, 0.65 m). Heights at 0.0428 m/px below the tip (y 557). Angles as for the raceways: from each spot's offset from the body's axis in photo_wdr (x 2647 above the flaps, x 2637 at the aft end; half-widths 117.5 and 127 px), with the camera looking along 143 degrees. Only the openings visible in this photo are placed; the far side isn't seen. The lowest sits on the ribbed skirt, so its decal is lifted over the rib sheet. Masks are plain generated shapes (refs/starship/port_round.png, port_square.png). Found by scanning the leeward side for small spots much darker than their surroundings (crops x 2500-2790, y 600-1780), then checking each by eye: the rest were raceway joints, hinge parts, the walkway and frost shadows. This photo shows no more dark openings on the leeward steel. Corrected (2026-10-28): the camera looks along about 143 degrees, not 130. The two raceways, which sit 40 degrees apart in this photo, are mirrored about the tower side (a scale model of the ship seen from the tower side, user's photo), so the camera is at 180 - (17 + 56) / 2 = 143 degrees; every angle read from this photo moves by +13 degrees.

aft_skirt.unit: m (z above the ship's base), degrees either side of the tower side
aft_skirt.source: photo_wdr (aft crop x 2500-2780, y 1560-1790, viewed at 3x): the leeward aft skirt is clad in fine vertical ribs, about one every 3 px (0.106 m at 0.0353 m/px across the aft end) from just above the base (y 1767) up to a band of hardware from y 1662 to 1613 (z 4.8 to 6.9 m). The band: a rim about 10 px (0.43 m) tall at the top with coloured vertical stripes, below it a row of dark slots about every 7 px (0.24 m), each about 0.08 m wide with a coloured fitting at its top. The windward side is tiled to the base (photo_s39_fire), so the ribs and band cover the leeward half only (+-88 degrees about the tower side, inside the tile edge). Line widths, cap and rim heights within a few cm estimated; the stripes cycle red, gold and steel.

aft_fittings.source: photo_wdr (aft crop): a stubby steel cylinder like the catch pins at x 2633, y 1667 (z 4.6 m), about 23 px (0.9 m) across and 1.4 m long, pointing almost at the camera (about 141 degrees). The other side is hidden behind the tower's walkway; taken as mirrored about the tower side, like the catch pins (assumed). Corrected (2026-10-28): the camera looks along about 143 degrees, not 130. The two raceways, which sit 40 degrees apart in this photo, are mirrored about the tower side (a scale model of the ship seen from the tower side, user's photo), so the camera is at 180 - (17 + 56) / 2 = 143 degrees; every angle read from this photo moves by +13 degrees.

aft_dome_panels.source: photo_ship_underside: the dome is a plate of bolted panels: long straight seams with rows of bolt heads along them (crop x 420-600, y 180-320). Seam layout estimated: radial every 15 degrees and rings at the dome's steps, bolts about 0.12 m apart.

bay_cables.unit: m; runs [[r, angle_deg], ...] along the dome, hanging `hang` below it
bay_cables.source: photo_ship_underside: two reddish-brown cables run from the skirt wall on the right across the dome to the sea-level engines (from about (575, 215) to (470, 260) and (520, 350), 245 px out of the 742 px skirt); the photo's angles are the model's plus 89 degrees (its vacuum bell 90 degrees from the flaps, at 91, matches the model's at 180). A third run on the other side assumed. Diameter estimated.

flap_actuators.unit: m: housing [radial, across, tall] on the skirt's inside wall at each aft flap (+y, -y)
source: spacex_v3: "The aft flap actuation system has also been upgraded from two actuators per flap to a single actuator with three motors."
photo_ship_underside: no actuator housing can be told apart from the brackets at the flaps' angles; placed inside the skirt behind each flap's root, above the brackets, and sized as a design value.

stainless_steel.source: photo_wdr, the leeward side of the ship's nose in daylight (native px about 2640, 820; 20 x 20 px averaged). The steel mostly mirrors its surroundings, so the colour is only a base; other samples were blue from the sky.

heat_shield_tiles.source: photo_s39_fire, the ship's windward side in daylight, four 24 x 24 px spots on the barrel averaged (from #080d14 to #1a1f2a).

port.source: photo_wdr, the large leeward port at x 2727, y 921 (7 x 7 px averaged).

aft_fitting_red.source: photo_wdr, aft hardware band (x 2560-2660, y 1613-1662): mean of the pixels with hue under 20 or over 330 degrees, saturation over 0.25 (36 px).

aft_fitting_gold.source: photo_wdr, aft hardware band (x 2560-2660, y 1613-1662): mean of the pixels with hue 25-60 degrees, saturation over 0.25 (28 px).

aft_hardware_dark.source: photo_wdr, aft hardware band (x 2560-2660, y 1613-1662): mean of the pixels darker than value 0.3 (398 px). Metallic and roughness estimated.

aft_dome_plate.source: photo_ship_underside, the aft dome's panels away from glare: (230-280, 250-290) #464c54 and (250-290, 440-470) #484f5a

bay_cable.source: photo_ship_underside, the reddish-brown cables across the aft dome at (450, 262) #494243, (470, 255) #6a6162 and (530, 235) #988585, averaged

open_questions: Ship height: 52.1 m is derived (124.4 - 72.3). The ascent photo gives 52.6 m (in ship diameters), agreeing; the pad photo gives 47.7 m but reads squashed vertically. Decided: 52.1 m.
Flap sizes and positions come from one photo each. Proposed: build from these estimates and compare the sheet with photo_pad_f13 and photo_f12_ascent.
Photos: SpaceX's licence for these isn't stated (their Flickr photos have been CC BY-NC 2.0). They stay out of the repo; the spec links them.
Not modelled: frost (only when fuelled), the docking drogues and Starlink antennas (too small at site scale).
Engines: vacuum bells sized from SpaceX's render of a nine-engine Block 3 ship; which three slots V3 fills and how the layout is clocked against the flaps isn't known.
Catch pins: the two cylinders on the forward section are taken to be the catch pins; nothing labels them.

items: Ship and booster as two separate models
